_notes: Planet surfaces for the game prototype (game/): a hex grid on 3D terrain. The game starts in orbit: the scan shows terrain and rough deposit hints per region; the player picks a landing site, the colony pod descends, and survey rovers reveal exact deposits as they drive. terrain: move_cost = effort to enter a tile (unit speed is effort per second); height = visual relief level. planets: per planet class, how a surface is generated. Elevation and moisture come from deterministic noise (feature_size = tiles per noise cell) and are ranked, so thresholds are shares of the map: elevation ocean 0.30 = the lowest 30% of tiles are ocean, below shallows = shallows, from hills up = hills, from mountains up = mountains, the rest is lowland; within lowland, moisture picks the terrain; polar_rows at top and bottom become polar_terrain. deposits: rolled per tile on matching terrain (coastal = must touch water); amounts are ranges. hints: region totals below likely = traces, below rich = likely, otherwise rich. landing: where a colony pod may set down (tile terrain, and every neighbour must be passable land), how long it falls, what it brings (start_stock, the hub building, units) and how far the landing reveals; assemble_seconds = how long the landed Colony Hub (and every outpost dropped from orbit) takes to assemble after touchdown: it stands on its tile but gives no output, power, storage, build range, build queues or repair pad until then (the vehicles can drive at once). build_menu: buildings the player can place on the surface (their costs and stats are in buildings.json: build_seconds, output_per_min, upkeep_per_min, extract_per_min, requires_deposit; the hub's build_radius and build_queues limit where and how many build at once). Tiles must be surveyed and buildable to build on. Power: power_resource (energy) is not stockpiled on a surface; each base (a colony core and the buildings in its radius) has a power budget: power_supply of its working buildings vs power_use; when use exceeds supply, every power user at that base runs at supply/use speed. Levels: a core upgrades along upgrades_to (Colony Hub 1 → Colonial Administration 2 → Planetary Capital 3), paying the next level's cost and taking its build_seconds; it keeps working meanwhile. Storage: stockpiled materials (everything except storage_exempt) share one capacity per player, the sum of storage on their finished buildings (the hub's vault, Storage Containers, refineries); mining stops when it is full. Hills and plains hold raw ore, which an Ore Refinery turns into metal. salvage_refund: share of the cost returned when a finished building is salvaged. units: speed = move effort per second; mark = which mark of a vehicle line it is (1-3: survey_rover is the Mk I Scout, survey_rover_mk2 the Mk II Surveyor, survey_rover_mk3 the Mk III Explorer); cost and build_seconds = what a Vehicle Bay charges and takes to assemble one; a unit with extract_per_min is a mining crawler: it unfurls on a deposit (deploy_seconds), fills a hopper and sends each full load home as a cargo pod that flies pod_speed tiles per second to the nearest storage building or refinery. breakdown: while mining, each minute has chance_per_min of a breakdown; the severity is picked by weight and knocks damage (a range) off its integrity (100 = perfect); an explosion also loses the load in the hopper. A broken crawler folds up, can't mine, and drives slower (down to slowest_drive of its speed at 0 integrity). repair: drive it onto a colony core's tile (the repair pad beside the hub); after crew_seconds (the repair crew walking out) it regains per_second integrity, paying cost_per_point for each point, until it is back to 100. damage (survey rovers): while driving, each terrain wears wear integrity a minute and has a hazard chance a minute (one of the hazards listed for that terrain, picked by weight, knocks damage off; a hazard with flat also punctures a tyre) and a flat chance a minute; a toxic tile corrodes toxic_per_min wherever the rover is, and on a predator tile wildlife attacks with chance_per_min (damage range); research with the breakdown stat scales the hazard and flat chances. found (the construction rover): founding a second outpost on the ground. The rover drives to a surveyed, buildable tile that is safe (no toxic ground, predators or native land), has no building on it or next to it and is at least min_distance tiles from the player's other colony cores (and from an outpost on its way down), parks and unfolds over deploy_seconds (paying cost as it starts; a move order folds it back up and refunds it), then is used up: building (a colony core) stands on the tile as a new base under construction, built by exocomps over that building's build_seconds in buildings.json using a build queue of its own; cancelling it before it is finished refunds cost and the rover rolls back out. min_distance is shorter than orbit outpost_drop.min_distance (8 vs 10: two Colony Hub build radii of 4, so the build areas never overlap) and the cost is lower than a drop (no drop ships; the panels come from the Vehicle Bay with the rover, and its crew drive over). Below slow_below integrity it drives slower, down to slowest_drive of its speed at 0; below sensors_below its survey radius drops by sensor_loss (at least 1); at 0 it is disabled: it stops, surveys nothing and only a repair order moves it, at crawl (also the slowest it ever drives). tyres: wheels (4 or 6; bit order front left, front right, [middle left, middle right,] rear left, rear right) and spares carried; the flat chance rises by low_integrity times the share of integrity lost; one flat drives at flat_speed, two or more at two_flat_speed, and each flat adds flat_wear (a share) to the terrain wear; the crew change a flat in the field in change_seconds parked (uses a spare, a move order stops it); a repair pad (crew_seconds walk, then) fits a new tyre on every flat and restocks the spares for pad_cost a tyre, then welds integrity back as for the crawler (repair). Any vehicle parked on its own colony core's pad that needs it is repaired. maintenance: buildings with wear_per_min lose that much condition (0..100) a minute while they work; below decline_below their output falls toward slowest_output at 0, and each minute they may break down outright (chance rising to break_chance_per_min_at_zero at 0); a broken building stops until maintained. Manual maintenance: the base's crew walks out (crew_walk_seconds + crew_seconds_per_tile per tile from the core), one job at a time per base, and restores repair_per_second, paying cost_per_point; buildings with auto_maintain (a top level, or the Automated Maintenance tech) fix themselves with drones whenever they drop below auto_below. research: surface techs a Research Lab works on (cost in research points; requires = techs needed first); modifiers add to building stats (speed, yield, wear) for the listed buildings (all buildings when none are listed), auto_maintain turns on drones, breakdown scales a unit's breakdown chance; ids shared with tech_tree.json are the same tech (deep_core_mining). orbit: the player's ship over the planet (name and ships.json class per faction), its cargo hold, and ways down: outpost_drop (a new Colony Hub at a safe site at least min_distance tiles from your other cores, after the first landing), shuttle (the drop ship: flies a payload unit down to a safe tile and goes back up), satellite (orbits over a band of band_rows rows and sweeps it every sweep_seconds, surveying it), transporter (levels by era, overridden per faction; range = tiles from your nearest base or unit, 0 = anywhere; cargo = supplies from the hold per beam; cooldown between beams). hud_resources: the stockpiled resources shown in the top bar, in order. unit_names: every new unit (landed, delivered or built) gets a name from pool and a number from the numbers range, in a random-looking order from the map seed; a player never gets the same name or number twice (when the pool runs out names go on as NAME II, NAME III...; when the numbers run out they go on with three digits). environments: per planet class, what the outpost's sensors read once its uplink to the ship is online (landing.assemble_seconds after touchdown): sky = the colour of the sky in the helm's surface feed; gravity_g; day_hours = the local day as shown on the clock, day_seconds = how long it lasts in game time; relief_km = altitude of the highest ground (land altitude rises with the cube of its elevation share above the ocean); temperature_c day/night = equator, sea-level afternoon high and pre-dawn low, polar_drop = how much colder the map's top and bottom rows are (rising with the square of the latitude), lapse_per_km = cooling with altitude; humidity_pct = the driest and wettest relative humidity (a tile's wetness from its terrain, biomass and water nearby picks within it, higher at night); wind_ms mean and gust; pressure_kpa at sea level, falling with altitude over scale_height_km (0 = no atmosphere); radiation_usv_h = surface dose rate in µSv/h by day and night (more at altitude and toward the poles); uv_index at noon; atmosphere_pct = the main gases, summing to 100 (empty for a vacuum); trace_ppm = trace gases; toxic_ppm = what a toxic patch (the biologics scan) adds to the air on it, fading over three tiles. telemetry: exposure_limits_ppm per gas (readings above it are flagged as hazards), breathable_o2_pct and breathable_kpa (outside = unbreathable), radiation, heat, cold and gust warning levels, and per terrain how much it scales the day/night temperature swing (swing), shifts the temperature (offset_c) and scales the humidity and the wind. Readings are pure functions of the data, the map, the tile and the tick (no dice rolls): a day/night cycle by the tile's longitude, slow weather noise and gusts. All numbers are placeholders.

research.name: Improved Smelting
research.effect: Refineries get 20% more metal from every load of ore.
research.description: Better furnace control and slag recovery pull more metal out of every load. Refineries get 20% more duranium and tritanium from the same ore, so each crawler load goes further.

research.name: Ore Conveyors
research.effect: Mines, deep-core mines and refineries work 20% faster.
research.description: Automated conveyor lines move ore from the drill heads into storage and from storage into the smelters, without crews hauling it by hand. Mines, deep-core mines and refineries all work 20% faster.

research.name: Preventive Maintenance
research.description: Inspection rounds and replacement schedules catch worn parts before they fail. Every building wears 30% slower, so breakdowns are rarer and the crew is needed less often.

research.name: Automated Maintenance
research.effect: Maintenance drones fix any building below 70% without a crew (parts still cost duranium).
research.description: Small maintenance drones patrol your bases and repair any building that drops below 70% condition, without waiting for the crew. Parts still cost duranium.

research.name: Alloy Metallurgy
research.effect: Alloy Foundries work 25% faster and get 10% more parasteel.
research.description: Refined alloy recipes and better crucibles for parasteel production. Alloy Foundries work 25% faster and get 10% more parasteel from each batch.

research.name: Reinforced Drills
research.effect: Mining crawlers break down half as often.
research.description: Tougher drill strings, shock mounts and better cooling for the mining crawler's rig. Crawlers break down half as often while mining.

research.name: Deep-Core Mining
research.effect: Unlocks the Deep-Core Mine: reopen a used-up deposit once at 50%.
research.description: Drilling techniques that reach past the depleted upper layers of a deposit. Unlocks the Deep-Core Mine, which reopens a used-up deposit once at half its original size.

units.description: Three officers with tricorders and a field kit, beamed or flown down from the ship. Slow on foot, but they survey the ground around them like a rover.

The Mk I Scout: a light four-wheeled rover with a sensor puck on a whip antenna. It reveals the exact deposits around wherever it drives, and it's the cheapest way to find ground worth mining. Two land with the colony. Rough ground (hills, ice, forest) wears it down and throws up rock strikes, sinkholes and flat tyres: below half integrity it drives slower, badly damaged its sensors reach less far, and at 0 it is disabled until it limps to a repair pad (R). A flat slows it (two flats: a crawl); the crew change one in the field with its spare (T), or a colony core's pad fixes everything.

The Mk II Surveyor: a six-wheeled rover with a spinning sensor dish. A little faster than the Scout, and it surveys a wider ring of ground around it, so it maps new land quicker. Like every rover it wears on rough ground, can hit hazards and get flat tyres (one spare on board, T to change it), and is repaired on a colony core's pad (R).

The Mk III Explorer: a long six-wheeler on big tyres with a sensor turret. The fastest rover, and it surveys the widest area, for long trips far from your bases. It needs a little dilithium to build. The toughest rover: it wears slower, hazards hurt it less, its big tyres puncture less often and it carries two spares (T to change one); repair it on a colony core's pad (R).

A tracked mining rig that drives to a deposit anywhere on the map, unfurls and mines it. Each full hopper flies home as a cargo pod to your nearest storage. It can break down while mining and is repaired on the Colony Hub's pad.

A heavy six-wheeler that carries a folded Colony Hub on its back: prefab wall panels, a crane to set them and an exocomp dock on the roof. Drive it to an open, surveyed site well away from your other bases (at least 8 tiles), press FOUND OUTPOST and pick the tile: it parks, unfolds its crane and lowers the panels (paying the founding cost), then its exocomps build the new Colony Hub around it. The rover is used up; cancelling the hub before it is finished refunds the cost and gives the rover back. It is slower than a Scout, barely surveys, and wears like any rover on rough ground (one spare tyre, T; repair on a colony core's pad, R).
